qnn-cascade-layers: Section 4.2, p.7: the paper defines the layered QNN as the cascade U(Theta) = U_L ... U_1 of variational unitaries. It is the survey's own description of the object, not a result.
garg-survey-scope: Abstract, p.1: 'we review and summarise the different schemes proposed to model quantum neural networks (QNNs) and other variants like quantum convolutional networks (QCNNs)'. The paper states its own scope. It makes no claim about the results of the work it reviews.
code-openly-available: Section 2, p.2: the authors state that their codebase is openly available on their GitHub repository. A statement about their own release.
contribution-vqaa-two-optimizers: Section 2, p.2: the contribution paragraph states that they implement the Neutral Atoms VQAA for the MIS in the docking setting, and that they use two classical optimizers and a graph machine learning approach. The wording 'significantly accelerate' is not in the value.
wmcp-formulation: Section 4.3, p.3-4, equation (1): 'The WMCP can then be defined as follows' with the objective, the constraints on the complement-graph edges and binary x_i. The value matches the equation.
hyperopt-parameter-bounds: Section 9.2, p.8-9: five parameters, rise plus fall time not above 5 microseconds, each 16 to 2500 ns, detunings between 0 and 8 rad/us. The value matches the text.
gini-score-threshold: Section 9.3, p.9: the Gini-based score (eqs 7 to 9) is the Hyperopt target, and 'if the Gini coefficient is less than 1/3, the result is deemed irrelevant, and the score is nullified'. The paper defines its own score.
gini-limit-fully-connected: Section 9.3, p.9: the authors state that the Gini measure does not guarantee a good or correctly distributed result and may not work for a fully connected graph. A limit on their own score. The result_type setup is right for a limit of a setup choice.
coelho-prior-work-difference: Section 10.1, p.9-10: the authors state that Coelho et al. explored similar aspects, that their own work was independent, and that their model and single-target choice differ. The paper states how its own work differs. It makes no claim about Coelho's results.
dataset-125-graphs: Section 10.2.1, p.10: the structures (lines, rectangles, triangles, triangular lattices, hexagons), spacings 6 to 11 micrometers, and the benchmark of 125 graphs, all as the text states them.
vqaa-target-generation-50-loops: Section 10.2.2, p.10: optimal parameters from VQAA with Hyperopt, loops 'averaging 50', and a second pass with increased depth for low scores. A statement of the authors' own procedure.
gcn-model-architecture: Sections 10.3.1 and 10.3.2, p.10-11: 5 GCN layers, hidden dimension 128, dropout 0.1, ReLU, add pool, a linear output layer, batches of 64, Adam with learning rate 0.01 to 0.0001, and a separate network for each target. The value matches.
adjacency-inverse-squared-distance: Section 10.2.3, p.10: 'computed as the inverse of their pairwise squared distance', with the exponent 'experimentally chosen through parameter optimization'. The text is slightly inconsistent (squared, yet an exponent is tuned). The value reports it as printed.
qaa-parameter-search-limit: Section 11.1, p.11: Omega and delta change drastically between problems (their figs 16 and 19), the grid search is slow but accurate, and the authors expect the difficulty to grow with scale. A limit the authors state about their own QAA runs. The scaling clause is their expectation, not a measurement.
scipy-vqaa-scale-limit: Section 11.2, p.12: they could not explore bigger instances given computational limitations, and the runtime grows and the scipy optimizer becomes unstable with graph size. Both are in the passage, and the Conclusion repeats the limit.
docking-graphs-not-representative: Section 11.5, p.14-15: 'The graphs used here may not be representative of real interaction graphs between molecules, which are at least twice as large for the smallest ones.' A caveat on their own proof of concept.
hackathon-origin: Section 14, p.16: the acknowledgment states that the initial development was created during the PASQAL hackathon, The Blaise Pascal [Re]generative Quantum Challenge. A statement about the origin of their own work.
embedding-bottleneck: Section 13, p.16: 'the current implementation bottleneck lies in embedding the problem into the register, presenting several challenges.' A limit the authors state about their own implementation.
scope-simulated-no-full-docking: Section 8.2 and Section 5: their results use Pulser simulation (figure 16 says all figures were obtained with Pulser). Section 12, p.15: 'Given our computational limitations, we were not able to compare a full molecular docking problem in a real-world application'. Both are the paper's own scope and limit.
qmla-mechanism-bayes-factors: QMLA section, p.2: the paper defines the protocol. It trains models by QHL, builds layers of a DAG, compares models by Bayes factors with an Occam-style penalty, and selects layer and global champions. Defined, not measured.
nv-two-qubit-mapping: Experimental set-up, p.2: the NV centre is represented in a two-qubit scheme, one qubit for the electron spin and the second encoding the whole environment (open system contribution). The model the authors use.
three-test-cases: Analysis, p.2-3: case (i) simulated data with random H0 and random probe phase, case (ii) simulation with a fixed H0 and fixed probe |++>, case (iii) experimental data with unknown H0. The value matches the three cases.
credible-models-definition: Analysis, p.3: the authors introduce four roughly equivalent 'credible models', in agreement with ab-initio models, and 'assert that QMLA is successful when these are found'. A success criterion the paper defines. The 86% rate is not in the value.
experiment-credible-100-instances: Figure 2 caption, p.4: the credible-model win rates in panel c are for 100 instances of QMLA each for experimental and simulated data.
two-qubit-bath-approx-limit: Analysis of the bath, p.4: the single environmental qubit is valid for the rapid fast-decay dynamics, but finite-bath effects are expected at the longer times probed by Hahn echo experiments. A limit on their own approximation.
qmla-greedy-spawn-9-params: Methods, p.8: 'The spawn rule employed in this work is a simple greedy search' and 'Here QMLA is limited to 9-parameter spin models with specific interactions.' The scope of their own runs.
qhl-resampling-defaults: Supplementary 1.3, p.12: Liu-West resampling with 'the Qinfer defaults, a = 0.98, lres = 0.5'.
champion-most-edges: Methods, p.8: 'the champion is the node at which most edges point, i.e. which wins the most pairwise comparisons.' The paper defines its champion rule.
reduced-model-bayes-100: Supplementary 1.5, p.15 (anchor confirmed: the text layer puts the passage on page 15, not 13-14): 'if this strongly favours the reduced model (B > 100), we prefer the simpler model'. The value matches.
sm5-cle-settings: Figure SM5 caption, p.26: CLE with 1000 particles along 100 epochs, repeated 150 times, for each number of spins.
qmla-requires-controls-simulator: Supplementary 1.7, p.15: QMLA assumes access to key experimental controls (the evolution time and the probe state) and to a trusted quantum simulator to test trial Hamiltonians. The paper states these as requirements on its own method.
search-space-combinatorial: Supplementary 1.7, p.20-21: the greedy inheritance rule cuts the models explored, but 'is clearly not enough to make QMLA tractable already for relatively small instances', and prior knowledge is needed. A limit on their own method. The result_type theoretical is loose: it is a stated limit of an informal scaling argument.
noise-cannot-disambiguate: Supplementary 2.2, p.25: 'it is here impossible to disambiguate all sources of noise' (projection noise and readout noise), and dedicated characterisation 'is beyond the scope of this paper'. A limit on their own experiment.
nv-sample-setup: Supplementary 2.1, p.23: home-built confocal setup at room temperature, 11 mT field parallel to the NV axis, electronic grade diamond with 4 ppb nitrogen and about 1.1% natural 13C.
poincare-single-spin-limit: Supplementary 2.4, p.26-27: a single environmental spin gives Poincare recurrence times short enough to appear in the simulated reduced dynamics, and the authors do not add phenomenological decay terms, to keep a time-independent model. Both clauses are their stated limit and choice.
gentile-qmla-bath-infeasible: Analysis of the bath, p.4: 'It is infeasible to apply QMLA to characterise the bath through a complete parameterisation, without a large scale quantum processor, as QMLA relies on the complete quantum evolution of the global system.' A limit the authors state about their own method.
assumption-2-pegasos-robust: Section 3, p.8 and Section 3.2, p.10: Assumption 2 is stated with its wording, and the paper says it 'is not mathematically proven' and that empirical evidence supports it (Appendix B.1). The paper states its own assumption and its status.
pegasos-delta-eps-relation: Appendix B.2, Lemma 9, p.29: stated with its definitions (epsilon = |h*(x) - h^N(x)|, delta = |f(w*) - f(w^N)|) and proved from Corollary 8, Cauchy-Schwarz and ||phi(x)|| <= 1. The rendered page shows epsilon <= sqrt(2 delta / lambda). The text layer drops the square root, so the quotes alone do not show it. Corollary 8 is proved from Lemma 7 in the paper.
lemma-7-strong-convexity: Appendix B.2, Lemma 7, p.27: stated and proved in the paper. The hinge-loss sum g(w) is convex, and f(w) minus (lambda/2)||w||^2 equals g(w), so f is lambda-strongly convex. Textbook tools only.
approx-qsvm-nonconvex-price: Section 1, p.3: 'The price to pay for this reduction in complexity is that the underlying optimization problem is non-convex and its solution therefore loses the guarantee of global optimality.' A limit the paper states about its own approximate QSVM.
approx-qsvm-conjecture-eps3: Section 4.4, p.15-16: the 1/epsilon^3 scaling is conjectured from the assumption of O(1/epsilon) steps (footnote 9: 'the theory is not applicable here'), and 'a rigorous proof ... remains an unsolved problem'. The paper states the limit itself.
approx-qsvm-training-setup: Section 4.4, p.16: SPSA with stochastic gradient descent on batches of 5, cross-entropy loss, M = 100, 1000 training steps, ZZFeatureMap and RealAmplitudes circuits. The value matches the text.
experiment-setup-8-qubits: Section 4.1, p.11: 8 qubits and 8 features unless declared otherwise, two settings (linearly separable and overlapping), and the Figure 3 feature map (H, Rz, ZZ, repeated 4 times).
complexity-definition: Section 1, p.2: 'The computational complexity of QSVMs is then defined as the total number of quantum circuit evaluations necessary to find a decision function which, when evaluated on the training set, is epsilon-close to the solution employing an infinite number of measurement shots.' The paper defines its own measure.
no-test-set: Section 2, p.4: 'throughout this work only a training and not a test is considered', with the focus on training, not generalization.
conclusion-eps-generalization-open: Section 5, p.18: epsilon is measured on the training set, and its relation to generalization error 'is an open question'. A limit on what the paper's epsilon results show.
conclusion-barren-plateaus: Section 5, p.18: for the approximate QSVM the global-optimum guarantee is lost, and one must also ensure the loss and initial parameters avoid barren plateaus. A caveat the paper states on its own approximate QSVM.
qsvm-scope-training-only: Introduction, p.2: 'we focus on the training of the QSVM and, hence, assume that the feature map ... has been chosen reasonably'. Conclusion, p.18: whether feature maps with a practical advantage exist is an open question. Both are the paper's own scope.
sg-of-qubo-is-energy-gap: Section 2, p.3: the Ising Hamiltonian is diagonal with the energies f_Q as its eigenvalues, so the gap of a Qubo instance 'is simply the difference between the lowest and second-to-lowest values of f_Q'. The paper defines the quantity it measures. 'Very hard to compute for large n' is a parenthetical aside in the quote. The remark about eigenvalues of Q is the authors' note.
sg-assumption-schedule: Section 3, p.4: 'Assume that f, g : [0, 1] -> [0, 1], f(0) = g(1) = 1, f(1) = g(0) = 0, f is monotonous decreasing and g is monotonous increasing', with f(s) = 1 - s and g(s) = s as the example. The conditions the paper states for its bound.
svm-qubo-assumption-alpha: Section 3.2, p.5: 'Following [14] we make the simplifying assumption that alpha_i can only take the values 0 or C', with alpha_i = C z_i, and the penalty term with weight lambda for the equality constraint. The paper states its own simplifying assumption.
cones-data-generation: Section 4, p.6-7: entries drawn i.i.d. from a triangular distribution on [0, 2w] with mode w, the second cluster shifted by 2w + D, then rotated and centered. The value matches the text.
qubo-scaling-norm: Section 4, p.7: 'To make SG comparable between Qubo instances of the same size, we scale each Q such that the infinity norm of Q = 1.'
conclusion-future-work: Section 5, p.11-12: only two Qubo formulations are compared. The authors say it 'would be insightful to compare the properties of more Qubo formulations of more problems in future work' and that the effect of Qubo parameters is an interesting direction.
gerlach-correlation-form-depends-on-kern: Section 4.1, p.8: 'Since different kernels are used in Fig. 4 and Fig. 5, the exact correlation form is dependent on the exact data set and the used kernel.' A caveat the authors state on their own measured correlations (quadratic for Cones, linear for Circles).
gerlach-experiment-setup: The corrected value is right (anchor confirmed). Section 4.1, p.7-9: 1000 data sets in each clustering experiment (figs 4 to 7), and the SVM margin figures 8 and 9 use the same configuration. Section 4.2, p.10-11: 10 000 data sets for the lambda and C figures 10 and 11. Three sizes n in {8, 20, 32} throughout. The 10 000 appears in the p.10 text and the p.11 captions.

theory_low.unitary-pauli-expansion: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section 4.2, p.6 states U = e^(iH) and the Pauli expansion of a Hermitian matrix as background for the QNN parametrization. It is not a definition the paper makes and it carries no proof.
theory_low.rydberg-vdw-r6-blockade: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section 5, p.4: the R^-6 scaling of the Van der Waals interaction and the Rydberg blockade are background physics the paper states without derivation or citation of its own result.
theory_low.pulser-analog-ising-hamiltonian: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section 5, p.4-5: that an array driven by one pulse is an Ising-like Hamiltonian (eq. 3) is background physics stated without derivation. It is the model the paper uses, but the claim 'can be represented as' is not shown in this paper.
theory_low.mwis-hamiltonian-equivalence: Section 6, p.5: the paper compares equations (4) and (5) by inspection and says they coincide at Omega = 0. No derivation is given, and the encoding is taken from cited work [18] and [20]. An informal match, not a proved result.
theory_low.bf-stable-under-smc: Supplementary 1.8, p.22-23: a stepwise derivation (Chebyshev, mean-value and Taylor arguments) but with no theorem statement. The conditions are qualitative ('sufficiently smooth', gradients 'not large', 'kappa d L is modest', gap 'at least comparable to B'). The precise particle bound is eq. SM28 and is not in the value. An argued bound with loose conditions, not a proved result as the value states it.
theory_low.qsvm-pegasos-bound-lambda: Section 3.2, p.10: the derivation takes the iteration bound T = O(1/delta) from the Pegasos paper [17] as a step, and rests on Assumption 2, which the paper does not prove (empirical support only, Appendix B.1). The printed formula is also garbled in the text layer. LOW: a proof using a cited result [17] under an unproved assumption.
theory_low.pegasos-delta-shots: Section 3.2, p.10: O(1/delta^5) and O(M^2/delta^3) both use T = O(1/delta), taken from the Pegasos paper [17], and Assumption 2, which is empirical and not proved. LOW: the derivation uses a cited result [17] as a step.
theory_low.lemma-5-shots-per-entry: Appendix A.2, Lemma 5, p.24-26: 'adapted from [4, Lemma 19]'. The proof uses Daniel's Theorem 4 ([34], [4, Lemma 16]), the bound E||alpha*|| = O(M^(1/3)) from [4, Remark 2], the noisy halfspace setting of [4, Lemma 14], and Latala's Theorem 3 through eq. (27). LOW: the proof rests on cited theorems. It holds only with fixed probability p > 1/2, and under Assumption 1.
theory_low.remark-6-improvement: Appendix A.2, Remark 6, p.27: a comparison with the cited result [4, Lemma 19] (R_tot = O(M^6/epsilon^2)). The claim of improvement depends on the cited work and is not proved here.
theory_low.kernel-error-operator-norm: Appendix A.1, p.23: the operator-norm bound (27) follows from Latala's Theorem 3, cited from [31, Theorem 2] and [32, Theorem 5.37], with the moment bounds (22), (24), (25). theory_low.sg-upper-bound-by-problem-gap: Section 3, p.4: the claim gamma(H(s)) <= min{gamma(HP), gamma(HI)} <= gamma(HP) is correct and follows directly from the endpoint conditions f(0) = g(1) = 1, f(1) = g(0) = 0, since H(0) = HI and H(1) = HP.
